GIS Lecture 2 · Narrated animation

From Datum to Projection

Two short narrated animations for the start of Lecture 2. Part 1 builds a datum, from latitude and longitude to the ellipsoid, the geoid and the datums used in North America. Part 2 flattens it onto a map: projection surfaces, distortion, and the coordinate systems in the Georgia lab data.

0:00 / 0:00

Transcript

Click a sentence to jump there. Keyboard: space plays and pauses, the arrow keys move one sentence, F toggles full screen.

    Voice: Microsoft Andrew (neural text-to-speech). Coastlines and countries: Natural Earth 1:110m via world-atlas; states and Georgia counties: U.S. Census Bureau via us-atlas. Ellipsoid and projection parameters are the published EPSG values; the datum shift at Tech Tower was computed with pyproj (NAD 27 to WGS 84, EPSG:1173). Geoid shapes, the flattening and the datum fits are drawn exaggerated, as the narration says. Companion labs: the Datum Lab and the Projection Light Lab.
